name: Evidence verse (shāhid)
definition: A verse of poetry, a verse of the Qurʾān or a saying of the Arabs quoted to prove a rule; plural shawāhid.
body: The books of grammar are built on their evidence: Sībawayh's al-Kitāb quotes about a thousand verses, and it is often said that fifty of them have no known poet. Later scholars wrote whole books on the evidence of the great handbooks: al-ʿAynī's al-Maqāṣid al-naḥwiyya explains every verse quoted in four commentaries on the Alfiyya, and al-Suyūṭī commented on the evidence of the Mughnī.
A shāhid is different from a mithāl, an example the grammarian makes up to show a rule (zaydun qāʾimun): the example teaches, the shāhid proves.
